brief: What we look for when hiring engineers in 2026 (it's not coding tests).

slots.author: Maya Patel
slots.headline: We Don't Do Coding Tests Anymore
slots.body: The best technical interview is a conversation, not an exam. Here is what we actually look for in 2026.

slots.author: Maya Patel
slots.title: System Design Over Syntax
slots.body: We ask candidates to architect a feature, not memorize algorithms. Clean trade-offs beat clever code.

slots.author: Maya Patel
slots.title: Communication Is a Feature
slots.body: Engineers who write clear docs and explain trade-offs ship faster. We test this in every interview.

slots.author: Maya Patel
slots.title: AI Fluency Matters Most
slots.body: We don't ban ChatGPT. We watch how candidates prompt, verify, and refine AI-generated output.

slots.author: Maya Patel
slots.title: Own the Problem End-to-End
slots.body: We look for curiosity about the 'why' behind the ticket. Ownership beats task completion every time.

slots.author: Maya Patel
slots.title: Learn in Public
slots.body: Tech stacks expire. We hire engineers who show proof of learning from failure and feedback loops.

slots.author: Maya Patel
slots.title: Culture Add, Not Fit
slots.body: We want diverse perspectives that challenge us. Hiring clones kills innovation and team resilience.

slots.author: Maya Patel
slots.headline: What Are You Looking For?
slots.body: Drop one trait you value most when building your engineering team in 2026.
